name: llama.cpp
one_liner: LLM inference in C/C++, built to run with minimal setup.
what_it_is: An LLM inference implementation in C/C++ whose stated goal is inference with minimal setup on a wide range of hardware. It supports integer quantization from 1.5-bit upward and hybrid CPU+GPU execution, which lets a model larger than available VRAM run by keeping part of it in system memory.
why_it_matters: It removes the assumption that running a model requires a datacentre GPU, which is what makes on-device and offline inference possible at all. The trade-off is quantization: you are trading measurable output quality for the ability to run, and how much you lose depends on the model and the bit depth.
suitable_for: Running a model on a laptop or a small server
not_suitable_for: High-concurrency serving, where a batching server uses the hardware better
Work where quantization loss is unacceptable and unmeasured
Teams who want a managed runtime rather than a binary to operate
